briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops $17B in Sales as Tax Relief Gains Traction; DEA and Psilocybin Momentum Build Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales even as operators fight the 24% wholesale tax — and for the first time, a leading gubernatorial candidate is putting real money and a repeal pledge behind relief. Nationally, rescheduling cleared another court hurdle, Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug got a fast-track FDA voucher, and MDMA therapy is back in front of regulators, signaling the psychedelics wave is far from over.

local.text: Michigan cracks $17 billion in lifetime sales — August alone generated roughly $259 million, pushing cumulative adult-use and medical sales past the milestone despite tax headwinds.
Jars Cannabis beats back surveillance mandate — after the chain blocked a court-ordered Flock camera in Madison Heights, the city backed down and the camera came down pending council approval.

GOP nominee pledges wholesale tax repeal — John James collected roughly $90,000 from industry executives and Michigan Cannabis Industry Association backing after vowing to repeal or slash the 24% levy.

Retail-only dispensaries gain edge over growers — as cultivation margins shrink under the wholesale tax, non-vertically-integrated retailers are picking up a competitive advantage over grow-heavy operators.
Industry presses unconstitutional-tax argument in court — MCIA's new lawsuit says the 24% wholesale tax creates illegal tax pyramiding beyond the 6% constitutional cap, teeing up potential relief.

national.text: Medical cannabis rescheduling survives court challenge — the D.C. Circuit declined to stay the Schedule III move, keeping medical marijuana's new status intact while opponents' suit plays out.
FDA fast-tracks Compass Pathways' psilocybin drug — COMP360 won a National Priority Voucher that could shrink review time to just 1-2 months, with NDA completion on track for Q4.
MDMA therapy resubmitted for FDA review — rebranded Resilient Pharmaceuticals (formerly Lykos) has filed a new drug application for MDMA-assisted PTSD therapy, reviving a shelved 2024 bid.
CLAIM Act targets cannabis insurance gap — the bill takes aim at the federal-state conflict blocking insurers from serving cannabis businesses even after rescheduling.

Court tosses $31.8M verdict against Curaleaf — the Sixth Circuit ruled a Michigan grower's cannabis supply contract was federally illegal, wiping out the jury award and underscoring the need for airtight deal structuring.
